title: Descent of one finite projective module over a directed ring colimit
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preorder and $F:I\to\mathrm{CommRing}$ a diagram with colimit $A$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For every finite projective $A$-module $X$ [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], there are $i\in I$ and a finite projective $F(i)$-module $M$ with an isomorphism $M\otimes_{F(i)}A\cong X$, where scalar extension uses the canonical map $F(i)\to A$.

source.place: Tag 0BC7, label more-algebra-lemma-colimit-perfect, first paragraph of the proof, using Algebra Tags 05N7 and 00NX

proof.text: Replace the directed preorder by its antisymmetrization. The quotient functor and a monotone choice of representatives give inverse equivalences of thin categories. Transport F and its colimit across this equivalence. A model at a representative stage, transported along the colimit ring isomorphism, gives a model for the original diagram.

A finite projective module X is finitely presented by Module.finitePresentation_of_projective. Apply the object clause of [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine] to obtain a finitely presented model M at a stage i and its base-change isomorphism to X. Finite generation and projectivity give a split surjection A^r → X from a finite free module, with a section, by Module.Finite.exists_comp_eq_id_of_projective. The module (F(i))^r is its canonical finite free stage model; tensoring its finite basis identifies its base change with A^r.

Transport the inclusion and retraction through the model isomorphisms, then use the map clause of [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine] to descend both maps. Choose a common stage above their stages and use the canonical iterated-base-change isomorphisms to compare their extensions. At that stage their composite becomes the identity after base change to A. The equality clause makes the composite equal the identity at a further stage. The resulting term is a summand of the transported finite free module, so it is finite and projective. Its base-change isomorphism to X is obtained by composing the previous isomorphism with the iterated-base-change comparison. Lift the index and isomorphism back from the antisymmetrization.
